To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the down-regulation in Met and ethylene pathways in roots and in nodules in response of drought stress is not related to the S availability, and (ii) the down-regulating effect of drought on Met biosynthesis is likely due to the inhibition of cystathionine-γ-synthase (CGS) activity.

drought stress provokes the decline in the expression and content of the enzymes involved in the methionine and S-adenosil-methionine biosynthesis pathways in M. Truncatula roots and nodule, and that the down-regulation seems to be a consequence of the reduced S availability in the plant tissues.

the down-regulation in the expression of enzymes involved in Met and ethylene metabolism in roots and nodulas may be a mechanism to limit the energy consumption of nitrogenase in drought-stressed legume plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible involvement of S metabolism in the regulation of symbiotic nitrogen fixation in M. Truncatula in response to water stress.
the regulation of Met and ethylene metabolism in M. Truncatula roots and nodule in response to drought.
the regulation of S and ethylene metabolism in legumes under drought conditions and the role of these metabolites in symbiotic nitrogen fixation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the drought-induced inhibition of nitrogen fixation in M. Truncatula is not caused by a limitation in Met availability, but rather by a down-regulation in the expression and activity of key enzymes involved in the Met biosynthesis and ethylene biosynthetic pathway.

the down-regulation in the biosynthesis pathway of ethylene, which in turn is related to Met and SAM metabolism, is a key factor in the regulation of symbiotic nitrogen fixation in Medicago trunculata plants under drought stress conditions.

the down-regulation observed for Met biosynthesis in M. tuncatula nodules under drought stress is a consequence of the drought-induced down-regulation of ethylene biosynthesis, which in turn results in the down-regulation in the expression of the key enzyme involved in Met synthesis, Met synthase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the drought-induced down-regulation of ethylene production is not a direct consequence of the drought-induced decline in Met and SAM biosynthesis.

water-deficit conditions induce the down-regulation, both in roots and nodulos, of the methionine biosynthetic pathway, which is likely responsible, at least in part, for the drought-induced decline in nitrogen fixation.

the drought-induced down-regulation of Met and ethylene pathways is a consequence of the inhibition of N fixation in nodules and that the down-regulation is not a consequence of the drought-induced inhibition of the S metabolism in the plant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the drought-induced down-regulation of ethylene and methionine metabolism in roots and nodulas may be involved in the regulation of nitrogen fixation under stress.
a reduction of the SAM and ethylene pools in M. tuncatula roots and/or nodules could be involved in the regulation of the symbiotic nitrogen fixation in response to water deficit.

the drought-induced inhibition of nitrogen fixation in M.  truncatula is not due to a shortage of S-containing metabolites, but to the down-regulation at the transcriptional level of the genes encoding the enzymes of the methionine biosynthesis pathway and the ethylene biosynthetic pathway.
